title: Chronicle Upgrade Operator and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Implement a robust operator (Chronicle) and an accompanying rollback playbook to orchestrate multi-stage upgrades for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers. The operator will coordinate binary and schema migrations, stage-specific health gates, LTS channel awareness, telemetry collection, and irreversible step detection. The goal is zero-downtime for control-plane upgrades where possible, safe migration for stateful services (DB, object stores, KV caches), and clear automated rollback paths when rolling back is the safest option. This ticket covers design, operator PoC, rollout gating definitions, and an actionable runbook for SRE/customer-facing engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Chronicle operator can orchestrate an upgrade across a 3-node control-plane and a 5-node compute pool with defined phases (preflight, canary, ramp, full) without manual per-node steps
Operator emits phase metrics and gate statuses that appear in Console rollout dashboard and triggers alerts on failure thresholds
Automatic pause on detecting migration drift (schema + binary mismatch) with clear CLI reason and remediation hints
Rollback playbook validated by tabletop exercise and automated dry-run that simulates a failed canary and executes rollback to previous LTS channel
Upgrade manifests and operator include LTS channel bindings so customers can opt into 'lts-stable' or 'lts-fast' tracks
All irreversible steps require explicit approval via Console/CLI and are logged to audit trail (KMS-backed signatures for private deployments)
design_notes: Chronicle is an operator that uses a declarative Upgrade CRD: desired_version, lts_channel, preflight_profile, gating_policy, migration_plan
Phases: PRECHECK -> PREPARE (quiesce, snapshot) -> CANARY (subset of nodes) -> RAMP (gradual percent) -> FINALIZE (schema migrations, cache invalidation) -> POSTCHECK -> COMPLETE
Use leader-elected coordinator per VPC cluster to avoid split-brain; leader leases recorded in cluster state with TTL
Migration plan will include ordered resource groups (control-plane, stateful DBs, object-store adapters, KV caches, runtime agents) and safe windows for paralellism
Idempotent migration runner: each migration step writes a migration checkpoint record to a ledger (append-only) to allow resume and deterministic rollback
Operator integrates with console rollout API to surface per-phase metrics and to accept manual gate approvals (OAuth-backed for Hosted; SSO/KMS-signed for Private)
rollout_plan: Preflight: run health checks, run compatibility matrix (binary X schema Y), verify backup snapshots uploaded to customer object store
Canary: target 10% of control-plane nodes + 1 tenant runtime node; run smoke tests and synthetic prompt throughput benchmarks
Ramp: increase to 50% then full if metrics within SLO windows
Manual Gate: require explicit operator approval for FINALIZE phase when irreversible DB migrations are present
Fallback: if any canary fails, abort ramp and trigger automatic rollback orchestration
Post-Upgrade Validation: run production-grade evaluation prompts and compare quality metrics against baseline for regression detection
migration_steps: Snapshot control-plane state and upload to configured object store (encrypted)
Lock schema migration mutex for DB cluster; run offline-compatible schema changes first (non-destructive), then deploy binary with feature flags
Drain runtime agents for per-node kernel cache warmup; apply KV cache version bumps with backoff
Run compatibility tests: model serving smoke tests, streaming tests, token-level latency/throughput checks
Apply destructive migrations only after manual approval and multi-region cross-checks
Rotate secrets where required and rotate keys in KMS using staging key and proof-of-rotation logs
preflight_checks: Disk space and disk I/O baseline check (must be >25% free)
Schema compatibility report (no-breaking-changes flag cleared / or flagged for manual review)
Backup existence and restore-test pass from the last 24h snapshot
Telemetry baseline: 95th percentile latency and token-cost baseline recorded
Network connectivity tests between coordinator and node agents
SLA implications calculated and emailed to customer contacts if expected maintenance window >10 mins
telemetry_and_observability: Phase and per-step metrics emitted via Prometheus: upgrade_phase, step_status, failed_step, affected_nodes
Console pulls rollout traces and shows token-level latency histograms during canary vs baseline
Automatic regression detector compares embed/response quality on canonical prompt-set using similarity and hallucination heuristics
Audit log entries for approvals, irreversible-step confirmations, and rollback triggers sent to customer's audit sink
Post-mortem template auto-created on rollback with attached waveform of key metrics
rollback_plan: Automated rollback will attempt to revert nodes to prior binary via operator-managed image registry tags and restore DB snapshot if migration checkpoint indicates irreversible change
If DB restoration required, operator will coordinate controlled restore to a parallel cluster then cutover after smoke tests
Rollback includes KV-cache invalidation and warmed caches on target rollback nodes
Final step: reconciliation run to ensure cluster state and version ledger match expected rollback version
If rollback cannot complete automatically, operator escalates to SRE with pre-populated remediation checklist and CLI commands
risks: Irreversible DB migrations could require long restores leading to customer downtime
Operator bugs causing split-decision between regions if leader election fails
Private deployments have heterogeneous environments; certain migration steps may behave differently on older kernels or custom storage backends
Telemetry gaps could delay detection of regressions during canary
Security: signing/approval flows must be airtight to prevent accidental irreversible steps
testing_plan: Unit tests for migration runner idempotency and ledger checkpointing
Integration tests on a multi-node emulated VPC environment (k8s + local object store) with injected failures
Chaos tests: simulated network partition during FINALIZE, ensure operator stalls and fails safely
Tabletop tabletop runbook exercise with SRE, Solutions, and PM to validate playbook clarity
Dry-run mode: operator simulates steps and produces a deterministic report without mutating state
